slides.title: Guarantee Means Container-Exact
slides.caption: Defines the QoS predicate used before exclusive allocation.

+package qos
+
+import (
+	v1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
+)
+
+// IsContainerEquivalentQOSGuaranteed checks if a container is considered Guaranteed
+// from the perspective of resource managers that allocate exclusive resources.
+// This requires the container to have both requests and limits set and equal
+// for both CPU and Memory.
+func IsContainerEquivalentQOSGuaranteed(container *v1.Container) bool {
+	// Check container-level CPU requests and limits are equal.
+	cpuRequest := container.Resources.Requests[v1.ResourceCPU]
+	cpuLimit := container.Resources.Limits[v1.ResourceCPU]
+	if cpuRequest.IsZero() || !cpuRequest.Equal(cpuLimit) {
+		return false
+	}
+
+	// Check container-level Memory requests and limits are equal.
+	memRequest := container.Resources.Requests[v1.ResourceMemory]
+	memLimit := container.Resources.Limits[v1.ResourceMemory]
+	if memRequest.IsZero() || !memRequest.Equal(memLimit) {
+		return false
+	}
+
+	return true
+}

callouts.note: requires equal CPU request and limit

slides.title: Admission Path
slides.caption: Pod scope now decides whether managers allocate once per pod.
bullets: [new] Topology Manager branches before container admission
[new] AllocatePod runs after a single pod hint
[risk] failed pod allocation rejects admission immediately

slides.title: Pod-Scope Admission Branch
slides.caption: Routes pod-level specs into the new one-time allocation path.

callouts.note: stores one best hint per container

callouts.why: A manager bug rejects the whole pod before containers can start.

slides.title: CPU Bubble And Empty Pool Guard
slides.caption: Rejects pods whose exclusive CPUs consume the shared pool.

callouts.why: Shared containers would escape NUMA affinity and run on node-wide CPUs.

slides.title: Memory Bubble Mirrors CPU
slides.caption: Applies the same shared-pool guard to memory resources.

callouts.why: A shared container with no memory allocation cannot start reliably.

slides.title: Checkpoint Migration Grows Up
slides.caption: CPU state migrates to V3 and persists pod assignments.

callouts.why: Container assignments intentionally survive; cleanup ordering needs reviewer attention.

slides.title: Runtime Pinning Queries Change Semantics
slides.caption: Exclusive CPU checks now ask the manager for isolation level.

slides.title: Node E2E Covers The New Surface
slides.caption: Tests verify allocations through podresources, not just specs.

slides.title: What Could Break
slides.caption: The review risk is mostly cross-manager consistency.

bullets.why: PodLevelResourceManagers assumes PodLevelResources is enabled wherever pod.spec.resources appears.

bullets.text: [risk] CPU and Memory guards must match
bullets.why: Divergent empty-pool handling would admit pods one manager cannot allocate.

bullets.text: [risk] checkpoint fallback hides corrupt V3 reads
bullets.why: A bad V3 read can fall back to V2, losing pod assignments until rebuild.
Insufficient NUMA or CPU topology can skip the exact cases reviewers care about.
